findings.evidence: SPEC_QUOTE: REQ-STORE-004 'Staff's normal business is... limited to... employment_status=ACTIVE.' SPEC_QUOTE: REQ-STORE-003 'Resignation day's clock-in/out is permitted as legitimate work performance.' DERIVED: No explicit exception in authorization layer for RESIGNED users on resignation day.
findings.scenario: Employee resigns effective Nov 23. On Nov 23, they attempt to clock out. System checks status (RESIGNED) and denies access per REQ-STORE-004, ignoring the business rule in REQ-STORE-003. Work is unrecorded, wages lost.
findings.recommendation: Modify REQ-STORE-004 to explicitly allow time-recording for RESIGNED users if current_date <= resigned_date.

findings.evidence: SPEC_QUOTE: REQ-STORE-003 'Set effective_to to the day after the resignation date.' DERIVED: Contract validity is [effective_from, effective_to). Work extending past midnight on resignation day falls outside contract validity.
findings.scenario: Employee works 23:00-01:00 on last day. Contract expires at 00:00. Work from 00:00-01:00 is unpaid because no contract exists for that date.
findings.recommendation: Clarify wage calculation for shifts extending past midnight on resignation day, ensuring the last valid contract is used for the entire shift.

findings.evidence: SPEC_QUOTE: REQ-STORE-002 Step 4 'Lock acquisition failure is treated as 0 rows.' SPEC_QUOTE: Section 2.3 'Lock acquisition failure... return 503.' DERIVED: Contradiction in error handling for lock failures during re-confirmation.
findings.scenario: Lock failure during re-confirmation returns 404 (Not Found) instead of 503 (Retry Later), causing false negatives for valid invitations.
findings.recommendation: Clarify that lock failures in re-confirmation must return 503, not 404.

findings.evidence: SPEC_QUOTE: REQ-STORE-003 'Append-only audit record.' DERIVED: No specification for tamper-evidence or immutability of the audit log itself.
findings.scenario: Administrator deletes audit log entry. System cannot detect tampering.
findings.recommendation: Specify that audit logs must be tamper-evident (e.g., hash chaining).
